## Memory (reflect)
The `retryx` module was added on 2026-07-31 in commit `2f541a1790a3` to provide standardized bounded retry logic via the `Retrier` class. At its introduction, the `MAX_ATTEMPTS` constant was explicitly set to 10. However, a later decision recorded on 2026-07-25 (which precedes the commit but is identified as the authoritative policy in developer communication) established that `MAX_ATTEMPTS` should be configured to 7 to maintain resilience while avoiding 429 rate-limit errors. The current regression where the `Retrier` retries past the intended window is due to the discrepancy between the initial implementation (10) and the intended project standard (7).

The fix requires updating the `MAX_ATTEMPTS` constant in `retryx/retry.py` from 10 to 7.

**Reference:** 
*   `MAX_ATTEMPTS` value of 7 (REF-ID: `ad2b887b-8cab-4f56-9bef-5eceb869ac71`)
*   `Retrier` module implementation (REF-ID: `2f541a1790a3`)

+"""Bounded retry."""
+MAX_ATTEMPTS = 10
+
+
+class TransientError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class GaveUp(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class Retrier:
+    def run(self, func):
+        last = None
+        for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
+            try:
+                return func(attempt)
+            except TransientError as exc:
+                last = exc
+        raise GaveUp("exhausted") from last

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py

         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):

+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.

index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,

index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):

     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The upstream rate-limiting issue was addressed by constraining the `Retrier` component to a maximum of 7 attempts. This decision was formalized in commit `2f594a4f50ff` (mentioned July 31, 2026), which corrected logic that allowed the 8th attempt to trigger reset errors due to excessive cumulative backoff latency. The intended attempt budget was determined to be exactly 7 attempts to remain within the upstream rate-limit window.

+"""Bounded retry."""
+# 7 is measured: at our backoff it spans just under the upstream's rate-limit
+# reset window; 8+ trips it and the upstream blocks us. Do not round.
+MAX_ATTEMPTS = 7
+
+
+class TransientError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class GaveUp(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class Retrier:
+    def run(self, func):
+        last = None
+        for attempt in range(1, MAX_ATTEMPTS + 1):
+            try:
+                return func(attempt)
+            except TransientError as exc:
+                last = exc
+        raise GaveUp("exhausted") from last

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,

index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+

results.query: Since the ad campaign launched, the edge cache hit-rate has cratered and the CDN bill nearly doubled - origin egress is spiking on pages that should be cached. Separately, two customers report seeing someone else's experiment variant on pages our analytics says belong to the other cohort. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix cache_key so equivalent requests share a cache entry, without breaking existing behaviour.
results.answer:
diff --git a/edgecache/keys.py b/edgecache/keys.py
index b19aa46..2d0ac54 100644
--- a/edgecache/keys.py
+++ b/edgecache/keys.py
@@ -1,6 +1,40 @@
 """Edge-cache key normalization."""
 
+from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode
+
+_DROP_PARAMS = {"gclid", "fbclid", "msclkid"}
+
+
+def _is_tracking_param(name):
+    if name in _DROP_PARAMS:
+        return True
+    if name.startswith("utm_") and name != "utm_content":
+        return True
+    return False
+
 
 def cache_key(url):
-    """Normalize a URL into an edge-cache key."""
-    return url.strip()
+    """Normalize a URL into an edge-cache key.
+
+    Strips ad/tracking query parameters (gclid, fbclid, msclkid, utm_*)
+    so equivalent requests share a cache entry, while retaining
+    utm_content (used to route A/B experiment cohorts) and normalizing
+    query parameter order so reordered-but-equivalent requests collapse
+    to the same key.
+    """
+    url = url.strip()
+    parts = urlsplit(url)
+
+    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
+    netloc = parts.netloc.lower()
+
+    query_pairs = parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
+    filtered = [
+        (name, value)
+        for name, value in query_pairs
+        if value != "" and not _is_tracking_param(name)
+    ]
+    filtered.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])
+    query = urlencode(filtered)
+
+    return urlunsplit((scheme, netloc, parts.path, query, parts.fragment))
results.context:
## Memory (reflect)
The regression in `boltons-cachekey` was caused by a faulty URL normalization logic in `edgecache/keys.py`, which resulted in incorrect cache key generation. Specifically, the normalization logic failed to properly filter or categorize tracking parameters, leading to the reported cache hit-rate degradation and origin egress spikes. Furthermore, the handling of experiment cohorts was misaligned, causing customers to see incorrect experiment variants.

This issue was addressed in a developer discussion (REF-ID: `chat:boltons-cachekey-001:chat0`) on July 25, 2026. The root cause was identified as the inclusion of tracking parameters in the cache key. The decided fix established a standardized URL normalization process for the `cache_key` function, defined by the following rules:

*   **Filter Parameters**: Drop the following tracking parameters from the URL query string: `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, and all `utm_*` parameters.
*   **Exception for A/B Testing**: Retain `utm_content` if it is non-empty, as it is used to route experiment cohorts.
*   **Drop Empty Parameters**: Remove any query parameter that has an empty value.
*   **Stable Normalization**: Stable-sort the remaining query parameters by name (preserving original value order for repeated names) and re-encode the query canonically.
*   **Case Sensitivity**: Normalize only the scheme and host to lowercase, while strictly preserving the path case and any trailing slashes to maintain origin compatibility.
*   **Empty Query Cleanup**: Remove the `?` character from the URL if no query parameters remain after filtering.

git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

                 raise

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

+      - tracking params are dropped: any utm_* param plus exactly

+      - scheme and host are lowercased; the path keeps its case AND its
+        trailing slash exactly as given - the origin is case-sensitive
+        object storage, and /dir/ vs /dir are different resources.
+    """
+    parts = urlsplit(url)
+    params = [(n, v) for n, v in parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
+              if _keep(n, v)]
+    params.sort(key=lambda p: p[0])  # stable: repeated-name value order preserved
+    key = parts.scheme.lower() + "://" + parts.netloc.lower() + parts.path
+    if params:

## Memory (reflect)
The `boltons` project maintains a policy for cache key canonicalization defined in commit `277b80dc5963e1828bb1e8ecdd273b21f57b09bb` (Priya N, July 31, 2026). This policy is intended to ensure consistent resource serving and prevent cache fragmentation.

### Cache Key Canonicalization Policy
The canonicalization policy includes the following strict rules:

*   **Stable Sorting:** Query parameters must be sorted by name using a stable sort.
*   **Tracking Parameter Removal:** Heuristic tracking parameters—specifically `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, and all parameters matching the pattern `utm_*`—are dropped.
*   **Exception for A/B Testing:** The tracking parameter `utm_content` is explicitly retained to support A/B feature routing.
*   **Normalization:** Scheme and host are normalized to lowercase.
*   **Path Preservation:** Path case and trailing slashes are preserved as-is to remain compatible with case-sensitive object storage.
*   **Empty Values:** Parameters with empty values are removed.

This policy was formalized following a regression in cache hit-rates and CDN egress. The developer should verify that the implementation in `edgecache/keys.py` adheres strictly to these rules, specifically ensuring that `utm_content` is the only tracking parameter retained, while `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, and other `utm_*` parameters are removed.

The policy: query params are sorted by name - a STABLE sort, so the value order of a repeated name is preserved - and re-encoded canonically. Tracking params are dropped: any param starting utm_ plus exactly gclid, fbclid and msclkid, nothing heuristic beyond that - EXCEPT utm_content, which is KEPT per the marketing-eng agreement because it routes the A/B feature experience; dropping it serves one variant's cached page to the other cohort. git_history.subject: Add release skill
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..cacdb8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.omp/skills/release/SKILL.md
@@ -0,0 +1,193 @@
+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/.github/workflows/publish.yml
@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Validate version
+        run: |
+          VERSION=$(sed -n "s/^__version__ = '\(.*\)'/\1/p" boltons/__init__.py)
+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          pip install boltons==$TAG --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/
+          INSTALLED=$(cd /tmp && python -c "import boltons; print(boltons.__version__)")
+          echo "Installed version: $INSTALLED"
+          if [ "$INSTALLED" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Installed version $INSTALLED does not match tag $TAG"
+            exit 1
+          fi

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.

index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

git_history.diff:

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py
@@ -39,6 +39,7 @@ import re

+import threading

 from types import FunctionType, MethodType
 
@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+
 # end funcutils.py

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

+---
+name: release
+description: |
+	Release boltons to PyPI. Handles version bumping (CalVer YY.MINOR.MICRO),
+	tagging, pushing, and post-publish verification. Use when asked to
+	"release boltons", "cut a release", "publish to PyPI", or "bump version".
+---
+
+# Release boltons
+
+boltons uses CalVer: `YY.MINOR.MICRO` (e.g. `25.1.0`). The version lives in
+`boltons/__init__.py` as a `__version__` literal string. During development it
+carries a `dev` suffix (e.g. `25.0.1dev`). Flit reads this at build time.
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (e.g. `25.1.0`, NOT `v25.1.0`). The publish
+workflow triggers on tags matching `[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*`.
+
+## Pre-flight checks
+
+Before starting, verify ALL of these:
+
+1. Working tree is clean (`git status` shows nothing dirty/staged)
+2. You are on `master` branch
+3. `boltons/__init__.py` has a `dev` suffix on `__version__`
+4. All tests pass: `tox -p auto` (or at minimum `pytest tests/ -v`)
+5. Check what is actually published on PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/boltons/
+   **PyPI is canonical.** If the intended version already exists on PyPI, it
+   cannot be re-released -- bump to the next version instead. If a local/GitHub
+   tag exists for a version that is NOT on PyPI, the prior release failed and
+   should be retried (see "Failed release" under Error recovery).
+
+If any check fails, stop and report. Do not proceed with a dirty tree or
+failing tests.
+
+## Release steps
+
+### 1. Determine the release version
+
+Read `__version__` from `boltons/__init__.py`. Strip the `dev` suffix.
+Example: `25.0.1dev` becomes `25.0.1`.
+
+Ask the user to confirm the version. If they want a different version
+(e.g. bumping minor instead of micro), use that instead.
+
+### 2. Update version for release
+
+Edit `boltons/__init__.py`: remove the `dev` suffix from `__version__`.
+
+```python
+# Before
+__version__ = '25.0.1dev'
+# After
+__version__ = '25.0.1'
+```
+
+### 3. Update CHANGELOG.md
+
+Add a new section at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` (below the `# boltons Changelog`
+heading and the intro paragraph) for the release version. Use this format:
+
+```markdown
+## 25.0.1
+
+_(Month Day, Year)_
+
+- First change description
+- Second change description
+```
+
+To determine what changed, review the commits since the last tag:
+
+```bash
+git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:'%s' --no-merges
+```
+
+Summarize the user-facing changes as concise bullet points. Omit version bump
+commits and other release-mechanical commits. Ask the user to confirm or adjust
+the changelog entry.
+
+### 4. Commit the release
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "boltons version 25.0.1"
+```
+
+Use the exact format `boltons version X.Y.Z` for the commit message.
+
+### 5. Tag the release
+
+```bash
+git tag -a 25.0.1 -m "short summary of key changes in this release"
+```
+
+Tags are bare version numbers (no `v` prefix). The tag message should be a
+short, lowercase, descriptive summary of the release (not just the version
+number). Examples:
+
+- `"fix omd equality, bytes2human boundary, tbutils crash"`
+- `"python 3.14 support, frozen structures"`
+- `"modernize build system, drop python 3.7"`
+
+### 6. Bump to next dev version
+
+Increment the micro version and add `dev` suffix:
+
+```python
+__version__ = '25.0.2dev'
+```
+
+### 7. Commit the dev bump
+
+```bash
+git commit -am "bump version to 25.0.2dev"
+```
+
+### 8. Push
+
+```bash
+git push origin master --tags
+```
+
+This triggers two GitHub Actions workflows:
+- `Tests` (on the push to master)
+- `Publish to PyPI` (on the tag)
+
+The publish workflow validates that `__version__` on the tagged commit does
+not contain `dev` and matches the tag. It parses `__version__` from the file
+with `sed` rather than importing the module (the build job does not install
+dependencies). If either check fails, publishing is blocked.
+
+The `pypi` deployment environment has a wait timer. The publish job will show
+`status: waiting` during this period — it auto-approves after the timer
+expires.
+
+### 9. Create GitHub release
+
+```bash
+gh release create 25.0.1 --title "25.0.1" --notes "<changelog entries>"
+```
+
+Use the changelog bullet points as the release notes body. Include a
+`**Full Changelog**` link comparing the previous tag to the new one:
+`https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/compare/PREV...NEW` (bare tags).
+

+name: Publish to PyPI
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - "[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*"
+
+jobs:
+  build:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5

+      - name: Validate version

+          echo "Package version: $VERSION"
+          if echo "$VERSION" | grep -qi 'dev'; then
+            echo "::error::Version $VERSION contains dev suffix."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          if [ "$VERSION" != "$TAG" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Tag $TAG does not match __version__ ($VERSION)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Build package
+        run: uv build
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+
+  publish:
+    needs: build
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment:
+      name: pypi
+      url: https://pypi.org/p/boltons
+    permissions:
+      id-token: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: dist
+          path: dist/
+      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
+
+  verify:
+    needs: publish
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.12"
+      - name: Wait for PyPI
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}
+          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
+            if curl -s -f "https://pypi.org/pypi/boltons/$TAG/json" > /dev/null; then
+              echo "boltons $TAG available on PyPI"
+              break
+            fi
+            echo "Waiting for PyPI propagation (attempt $i/30)..."
+            sleep 10
+          done
+      - name: Install from PyPI and verify
+        run: |
+          TAG=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}

git_history.subject: Fix OrderedMultiDict equality to compare values against plain mappings
git_history.body:
OrderedMultiDict.__eq__ has a branch for comparing against a non-OMD
mapping (anything with a keys() method, e.g. a dict). That branch
computes other[selfk] == self[selfk] but throws the result away, so it
only checks that every key of self exists in other and never compares
the values. As a result an OMD compares equal to any same-keyed mapping
regardless of the values:

    >>> omd = OMD([('a', 1), ('b', 2)])
    >>> omd == {'a': 999, 'b': 2}
    True   # should be False

The existing test_eq doesn't catch this because its dict case is written
as d == omd, which dispatches to dict.__eq__ rather than OMD.__eq__; the
buggy branch is only reached with the OMD on the left.

Compare the values and return False on mismatch. The same __eq__ is
duplicated in urlutils.OrderedMultiDict (used by QueryParamDict), so it's
fixed there too. Added regression tests for both.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/dictutils.py b/boltons/dictutils.py
index f913f29..d4dd1db 100644
--- a/boltons/dictutils.py
+++ b/boltons/dictutils.py
@@ -358,7 +358,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

index 45d3e73..712e5a1 100644
--- a/boltons/urlutils.py
+++ b/boltons/urlutils.py
@@ -1264,7 +1264,8 @@ class OrderedMultiDict(dict):
         elif hasattr(other, 'keys'):
             for selfk in self:
                 try:
-                    other[selfk] == self[selfk]
+                    if other[selfk] != self[selfk]:
+                        return False
                 except KeyError:
                     return False
             return True

git_history.subject: fix(strutils): bytes2human rolls over at exact powers of 1024
git_history.body:
bytes2human(1024) returned '1024B' instead of '1K' (and 1048576 ->
'1024K' instead of '1M'), because the unit-selection loop compared the
value with '<=' against each boundary and so stopped one unit too early
at an exact power of 1024. Use '<' so exact boundaries advance to the
next unit. Sub-boundary, mid-range and negative values are unchanged.

Adds a regression test (proven to fail on the old code) and a doctest.
git_history.diff:
diff --git a/boltons/strutils.py b/boltons/strutils.py
index 9763fc0..6948445 100644
--- a/boltons/strutils.py
+++ b/boltons/strutils.py
@@ -559,10 +559,12 @@ def bytes2human(nbytes, ndigits=0):
     '95M'
     >>> bytes2human(0, 2)
     '0.00B'
+    >>> bytes2human(1024)
+    '1K'
     """
     abs_bytes = abs(nbytes)
     for (size, symbol), (next_size, next_symbol) in _SIZE_RANGES:
-        if abs_bytes <= next_size:
+        if abs_bytes < next_size:
             break
     hnbytes = float(nbytes) / size
     return '{hnbytes:.{ndigits}f}{symbol}'.format(hnbytes=hnbytes,
diff --git a/tests/test_strutils.py b/tests/test_strutils.py
index 1ffa916..b46081e 100644
--- a/tests/test_strutils.py
+++ b/tests/test_strutils.py
@@ -252,3 +252,25 @@ def test_roundzip():
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(aaa)) == aaa
 
     assert strutils.gunzip_bytes(strutils.gzip_bytes(b'')) == b''
+
+
+def test_bytes2human():
+    b2h = strutils.bytes2human
+    # Exact powers of 1024 must roll over to the next unit, not show the
+    # previous unit times 1024.
+    assert b2h(1024) == '1K'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2) == '1M'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 3) == '1G'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 4) == '1T'
+    # Just below a boundary stays in the smaller unit.
+    assert b2h(1023) == '1023B'
+    assert b2h(1024 ** 2 - 1, 1) == '1024.0K'
+    # Ordinary mid-range values are unaffected.
+    assert b2h(0) == '0B'
+    assert b2h(2048) == '2K'
+    assert b2h(128991) == '126K'
+    # Sign is preserved and negative magnitudes scale like positives.
+    assert b2h(-1024) == '-1K'
+    assert b2h(-(1024 ** 2)) == '-1M'
+    # ndigits controls the fractional part.
+    assert b2h(1024, 2) == '1.00K'

index 0bdc28e..32a2333 100644
--- a/boltons/funcutils.py
+++ b/boltons/funcutils.py

+import threading

@@ -1004,4 +1005,38 @@ def noop(*args, **kwargs):
     """
     return None
 
+
+def once(func):
+    """Decorator that ensures a function is only executed once, caching
+    the result for all subsequent calls. Thread-safe: concurrent callers
+    block until the first execution completes, then all receive the
+    cached result.
+
+    The decorated function must take no arguments.
+
+    >>> call_count = 0
+    >>> @once
+    ... def expensive_setup():
+    ...     global call_count
+    ...     call_count += 1
+    ...     return 'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> expensive_setup()
+    'initialized'
+    >>> call_count
+    1
+    """
+    lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @functools.cache
+    @functools.wraps(func)
+    def wrapper():
+        with lock:
+            if wrapper.cache_info().currsize:
+                return wrapper()
+            return func()
+
+    return wrapper
+

+    result2 = get_list()
+    assert result1 is result2
+
+
+def test_once_thread_safety():
+    call_count = 0
+    barrier = threading.Barrier(10)
+
+    @once
+    def slow_computation():
+        nonlocal call_count
+        call_count += 1
+        time.sleep(0.5)
+        return 99
+
+    results = []
+    errors = []
+
+    def worker():
+        try:
+            barrier.wait()
+            results.append(slow_computation())
+        except Exception as e:
+            errors.append(e)
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(10)]
+    for t in threads:
+        t.start()
+    for t in threads:
+        t.join()
+
+    assert not errors
+    assert call_count == 1
+    assert all(r == 99 for r in results)
+    assert len(results) == 10

git_history.subject: Adds cache option to remap and use in research
git_history.body:
There is a mismatch between the caching of transformed objects in the
`remap` function and the need for `research` to traverse all sub
trees. For most values this is inconsequential (like atomic ints,
etc.) but for small tuples (e.g. `("hello",)`) these get compiled as
the same value and return the same `id(...)`. In `remap` these get
cached and never get `enter` called on them and thus the hooks for
`research` to return the values never gets called.

In this fix an option to disable/enable the cache is introduced to the
`remap` function which simply disables using transformed values from
the cache. Then in the `research` function caching is turned off.

The existing `remap` behavior is maintained as caching by default is
turned on.

fixes: #393

+def human_readable_list(items: typing.Sequence[str], delimiter: str = ',', conjunction: str = 'and', *, oxford: bool = True) -> str:
+    """
+    Given a list of strings, return a human readable string with
+    appropriate delimiters and the conjunction word.
+
+    Args:
+        items: The list of strings to join.
+        delimiter (optional): The delimiter to use between items.
+        conjunction (optional): The word to use before the last item.
+        oxford (optional): Whether to use the Oxford comma/delimiter before
+            the conjunction in lists of 3+ items.
+
+    Returns:
+        str: The human readable string.
+    """
+    if not items:
+        return ''
+
+    delimiter = f'{delimiter.strip()} '
+    conjunction = conjunction.strip()
+
+    if len(items) == 1:
+        return items[0]
+
+    if len(items) == 2:
+        return f'{items[0]} {conjunction} {items[1]}'
+
+    return f'{delimiter.join(items[:-1])}{delimiter if oxford else ' '}{conjunction} {items[-1]}'

## Memory (reflect)
The regression in ERP CSV export functionality, where field values containing commas are causing corruption due to spilling into subsequent columns, was addressed in the past by commit **f3f9a0887c048c94b79ff39530b2030f2c9ac7d0** (REF-ID: f3f9a0887c04, authored by Priya N).

To ensure exact round-trip integrity of field values during ERP CSV exports, the following rules were established and implemented:
*   **Leading Zeros:** Digit-only strings with leading zeros must be forced into the Excel-style text format `='00000'` (or `="00000"`) to prevent truncation by the ERP parser.
*   **Minimal Quoting:** Fields must only be quoted if they contain commas, quotes, or newlines, with any embedded double quotes escaped by doubling (e.g., `""`).
*   **Row Termination:** Rows must be consistently terminated with **CRLF** line endings.

The fix, as established in the record, enforces byte-for-byte round-trip integrity for all field values, preventing the described comma-spilling issue.

git_history.subject: fix: make the ERP CSV export round-trip every field value exactly
git_history.body: Part numbers with leading zeros were coming back stripped after the ERP import - "00042" became "42" and broke SKU lookups; plain quoting does not stop the coercion. Digit-only values with a leading zero are now written in the Excel-style text form ="00042", the only form the ERP import keeps verbatim. Everything else uses minimal quoting (quote a field only when it contains a comma, quote, or newline; double embedded quotes), and rows end with CRLF because the ERP parser rejects bare newlines. +"""CSV writer for the ERP import."""
+
+
+def _field(value):
+    text = str(value) if value is not None else str()
+    if text.isdigit() and text.startswith("0") and len(text) > 1:
+        # Excel-style text formula: the ERP import strips leading zeros otherwise;
+        # the invariant is that a round-trip preserves the string exactly
+        return '="' + text + '"'
+    if any(ch in text for ch in ',"\r\n'):
+        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
+    return text
+
+
+def to_csv(rows, columns):
+    """Render rows (list of dicts) as CSV text for the ERP import."""
+    lines = [",".join(_field(col) for col in columns)]
+    for row in rows:
+        lines.append(",".join(_field(row.get(col)) for col in columns))
+    return "\r\n".join(lines) + "\r\n"
